# Afrikaans translation sheet

<!-- Generated by `pnpm gen:i18n:sheet` (scripts/guards/i18n_sheet.mjs). Don’t edit by hand: `pnpm check:i18n` and the catalogue tests fail when it drifts. -->

Every string a farmer can see in the app that has no reviewed Afrikaans yet (roadmap WP-2.5). Until a string
is translated, the app shows it in English. Please fill in the **Afrikaans** column and send the sheet back;
a developer copies each line into the catalogue by its **Id**, and the line then leaves this sheet.
A site string's id is made from its English: if the English changes, the string comes back with a new id.

How to write the Afrikaans:

- Keep every `{name}` placeholder as it is (the app fills it in: a number, a date, a farm name). You may move it.
- Keep `**` round the words that should stay bold.
- Ids ending in `.one` / `.other` are the singular and plural of one word; `.two` / `.few` are ordinal forms.
- A row whose context starts **Meaning:** has English that means something else elsewhere; each has its own row, so they can be worded differently.
- The farm pages use plain words, not a modeller’s; `docs/design/farmer-view.md` §5.1 lists the words to use and the ones to avoid, with a first draft in Afrikaans for the reviewer.
- Numbers, dates and units are formatted by the app; don’t translate them.

604 strings: 510 on the site, 70 in emails, 24 in the glossary.

### mail.alert

Alert emails (WP-2.13): sent when a figure crosses a line the WUA set (a farm dam running low, the WUA’s restriction notice). Worded as what the model estimates, never as a promise or an order. {what} is one of the “what” lines; {date} and {madeOn} are dates like “3 Oct 2026”; {pct} and {threshold} are percentages like “28 %”.

## Glossary

### help

The glossary, “What do these words mean?”, linked from every farm page. Plain words for farmers.

| Id | English | Context | Afrikaans |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `help.farm-even-share.term` | Even share | The entry’s title. (For the developer: sourceHash 12fb005bdc918fadd911d84f03a437ee73e2321ad9de86f2a4f959dd902c1296.) |  |
| `help.farm-even-share.short` | The share of what they needed that farms across the catchment received. A fairness check, not water you are owed. | One sentence, shown first (at most 140 characters). |  |
| `help.farm-even-share.long` | Add up what every farm in the catchment needed, and what they all received. The even share is the second as a part of the first: if it is 89 %, farms together received 89 % of what they needed.<br><br>Your farm page puts your own figure next to it, so you can see whether you did a little better or worse than the catchment as a whole. It is a fairness check, not extra water for you: whether more water can reach your farm depends on where you are on the river and what is in your dam.<br><br>It is only shown when there are enough farms in the catchment that it can’t reveal a neighbour’s figures. | The fuller explanation; <br><br> is a new paragraph. |  |
| `help.farm-reserve.term` | The river’s reserve | The entry’s title. (For the developer: sourceHash 56a2c9107ea1ce62d7d160fe7c2e80c8ba9ed4ea9d4c080838f59dc39320303c.) |  |
| `help.farm-reserve.short` | Water the law keeps in the river so it stays healthy for everyone downstream. | One sentence, shown first (at most 140 characters). |  |
| `help.farm-reserve.long` | South African law sets aside some water in every river: the Ecological Reserve. The model checks, day by day, whether the river kept that much water at the outlet and at the gauges below your farm.<br><br>On days it didn’t, the farms upstream are asked to make it up, each in proportion to the water it used up or stored. Water that flows back to the river doesn’t count against you. On some days the river was low only because of low rain; those days ask nothing of anyone. | The fuller explanation; <br><br> is a new paragraph. |  |
| `help.farm-pump-less.term` | Pump less (for the river) | The entry’s title. (For the developer: sourceHash b7937f7ab02e4b369a129bdda40a92fbd415b586417a6fe4bbe777a7ca9d0fee.) |  |
| `help.farm-pump-less.short` | How much less you would have pumped on the days the river needed water, so it kept its reserve. | One sentence, shown first (at most 140 characters). |  |
| `help.farm-pump-less.long` | Your farm page gives this per day the river needed it, not averaged over the whole season: cutting a little every day does little on the days that matter.<br><br>If your dam also held back water the river needed, the page says so separately. That part isn’t taken off your pumping; if your dam has an outlet or a bypass, letting that water through helps.<br><br>This is the model’s estimate. Only a notice from your WUA is a restriction. | The fuller explanation; <br><br> is a new paragraph. |  |
| `help.farm-modelled.term` | Modelled (worked out by the model) | The entry’s title. (For the developer: sourceHash ded564c2423cd82906cc132c994961e5dc58bd65660a6026c9c2db17cf18ed9b.) |  |
| `help.farm-modelled.short` | Worked out by a computer model of the catchment from rain, river flow and crops, not read from a meter or gauge. | One sentence, shown first (at most 140 characters). |  |
| `help.farm-modelled.long` | Nobody measures your dam or your pump for this page. The model works out every day how much rain fell, how much water flowed down the river to your farm, what your crops needed and what your dam held.<br><br>It can be wrong. If your meter or gauge plate reads very differently, tell your WUA: it helps them correct the model. | The fuller explanation; <br><br> is a new paragraph. |  |
| `help.farm-needed.term` | Water you needed | The entry’s title. (For the developer: sourceHash a3d3b9f5fca5ee5462f7fda6adb105cc6f463fa988412dc1a0123cf9be0b2ac2.) |  |
| `help.farm-needed.short` | What your farm would have to pump for its crops: what the crops use, allowing for the water lost on the way. | One sentence, shown first (at most 140 characters). |  |
| `help.farm-needed.long` | Crops need a certain amount of water each day, less what the rain gives them. Not all the water you pump reaches the crop: some is lost to wind, evaporation and run-off. The model allows for that with your irrigation system’s efficiency (drip about 90 %, micro or centre pivot 85 %, sprinklers 75 %, flood 65 %).<br><br>So "needed" is what you would have to pump, the quantity your meter shows. If the page names the wrong irrigation system for your farm, tell your WUA. | The fuller explanation; <br><br> is a new paragraph. |  |
| `help.farm-stop-level.term` | Stop level | The entry’s title. (For the developer: sourceHash 3a36166dd04a0856af9d3dc3183a21509dd7b4875f506eace83e72788ff25507.) |  |
| `help.farm-stop-level.short` | The dam level where irrigation stops: your pump intake, or water you keep back. The model won’t irrigate below it. | One sentence, shown first (at most 140 characters). |  |
| `help.farm-stop-level.long` | "You can still use" is the water in your dam above this level. The days-left line divides it by what you used over the last 14 days, as a rough guide if nothing flows in.<br><br>If the page says the model assumes your pump can empty the dam, no stop level is set for your farm yet: tell your WUA the level your pump stops at. | The fuller explanation; <br><br> is a new paragraph. |  |
| `help.farm-model-band.term` | Model: OK, watch or short | The entry’s title. (For the developer: sourceHash aacaa9467417def76b6cdb571cc957bd0c65b683504244df0509cd5671f4a9b9.) |  |
| `help.farm-model-band.short` | The model’s own rating of your season so far. Not a restriction: only a notice from your WUA is one. | One sentence, shown first (at most 140 characters). |  |
| `help.farm-model-band.long` | OK: you would have had at least 90 % of the water you needed after pumping less for the river. Watch: 70 to 90 %, or your dam held back water the river needed. Short: under 70 %.<br><br>These thresholds are a proposal the WUA may change. | The fuller explanation; <br><br> is a new paragraph. |  |
| `help.farm-saved-copy.term` | The copy kept on your phone | The entry’s title. (For the developer: sourceHash 6cfcf9b3943e90fe604d0510c0f187b1d5376d22e433f0dd68186ca59ed9a4b4.) |  |
| `help.farm-saved-copy.short` | Your farm’s last figures, kept on this phone so they show at once and when there is no signal. | One sentence, shown first (at most 140 characters). |  |
| `help.farm-saved-copy.long` | It holds only your own farm’s figures, which you may see anyway. It is removed when you sign out, when someone else signs in on this phone, when you no longer have access to the farm, and when it hasn’t been opened for 30 days.<br><br>On a phone you share, choose "Don’t keep a copy on this phone" in the Menu. | The fuller explanation; <br><br> is a new paragraph. |  |
